detail.title: The End of the Fabless Illusion: A Thermodynamic Approach to Phase Transitions in Asset-Light Models and the Mark-to-Market Trap
detail.abstract: Joseph Schumpeter once prophesied the self-destruction of capitalism through its own success. However, in the 20th century, he could not calculate the thermodynamic limits of the "physical exhaust" (environmental destruction and labor exploitation) caused globally by modern financial capitalism. Utilizing the MVE (Multi-layered Value Evaluation) model, this paper redefines the highly praised "asset-light" business models of today's tech giants not as pure economic efficiency, but as a "Thermodynamic Value-Extraction System." Their astronomical market capitalizations are fictions maintained exclusively through three processes: 1) Structural hollowing-out of domestic infrastructure (Intake), 2) Institutional hacking of foreign capital defenses via Mark-to-Market accounting (Catalyst), and 3) Extreme negative externalities forced upon both the domestic working class and the Global South (Exhaust). As geopolitical fragmentation clogs this "exhaust pipe," we prove mathematically that the onset of the "Terminal Cash Constraint" will force a violent phase transition from speculative premiums to an "Ultimate Solvency" backed by physical reality.

title: The Dismantling of the Hard Asset Myth and the Stripping of Synthetic Premiums: Contradictions of the LBMA System and Gold Price Collapse under the Terminal Cash Constraint
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Dismantling of the Hard Asset Myth and the Stripping of Synthetic Premiums: Contradictions of the LBMA System and Gold Price Collapse under the Terminal Cash Constraint
detail.abstract: This paper highlights structural flaws in the price formation mechanism of gold-traditionally perceived as an absolute hard asset and an inflation hedge-and discusses the probability of a price collapse during an impending systemic liquidity crisis. First, we falsify the premise of "physical scarcity" using data demonstrating that Russia's unilateral production volume alone far exceeds annual industrial demand, compounded by over 600 years' worth of above-ground inventory. Second, utilizing the 2022 sanction events as empirical evidence, we demonstrate that the majority of the current gold price is not intrinsic value, but rather a "Synthetic Premium" reliant on LBMA (London Bullion Market Association) Good Delivery certification. Finally, we propose a mechanism wherein, as the macroeconomic environment approaches a Terminal Cash Constraint (TCC: ϕ → 0), the current All-In Sustaining Costs (AISC) will fail to act as a price floor. Instead, a Liquidity-Driven Fire Sale, triggered by the unwinding of abnormal leverage in paper markets (e.g., COMEX), will precipitate a nonlinear collapse of the gold price toward its true physical limit (P physical).

title: Did Learners Make Better Decisions After Seeing the Data? The Decision Evidence Framework for Experiential Business Education

detail.title: Did Learners Make Better Decisions After Seeing the Data? The Decision Evidence Framework for Experiential Business Education
detail.abstract: Experiential learning is often praised for improving engagement and practical understanding, yet educators still face a persistent question: did learners actually make better decisions after encountering relevant business data? This teaching note introduces the Decision Evidence Framework (DEF), a conceptual model for making learning more visible in experiential business education. The framework proposes that learning evidence can be observed not only in final outputs, but also in how learners make decisions, observe consequences, receive feedback, and then revise, defend, or improve their judgment after exposure to new information. The paper argues that this question has become even more important in an era when generative AI can help students produce polished outputs that may not reliably reveal underlying reasoning. Using a digital business simulation context as illustration, the note explains how structured experiential environments can turn decisions, outcomes, feedback, and reflection into more visible evidence of learning over time. In the present case, the discussion is illustrated through MonsoonSIM, but the framework is intended to be transferable across experiential learning settings.

title: First Connection to Nepal's Primary Road Network and District Development
affiliations: George Mason University

detail.title: First Connection to Nepal's Primary Road Network and District Development
detail.abstract: This paper studies whether first connection to Nepal's primary road network altered district development between 1971 and 2011. I reconstruct the first census year in which each district entered the national primary road system and combine this chronology with a harmonized district census panel. The main estimates use a staggered difference-indifferences design that compares newly connected districts with districts that are not yet connected. First connection is associated with a shift out of agriculture and into nonagricultural employment, especially services. The same pattern appears in a structural-transformation ratio that measures manufacturing plus service employment relative to agricultural employment, and in a log transformation of that ratio. The corresponding literacy response is small and not precisely tied to connection timing. The evidence suggests that primary roads were linked to Nepal's gradual shift away from agricultural employment, but with the caveats that roads were not placed randomly, district boundaries changed over time, and road expansion often came alongside broader state activity.

title: Does Decentralization Work Under Declining Local Population? Evaluation of Japanese Long-Term Care Policy
affiliations: Tokyo University of Science and Nanzan University

detail.title: Does Decentralization Work Under Declining Local Population? Evaluation of Japanese Long-Term Care Policy
detail.abstract: Rapid population aging has exposed several countries to the risk of population decline. In this context, can decentralization, which has yielded positive outcomes in many economic fields, function effectively under conditions of local population shrinkage? To answer this question, we evaluate a decentralization policy for public long-term care insurance in Japan, where population decline, especially in rural areas, is already underway. The policy transferred the role of setting the content and prices of covered care services from the central government to lower-level local authorities. At the same time, the policy encouraged to accept care providers with lower qualifications to reduce costs. Using nationally-representative individual-level data generated from administrative records, we employ a staggered difference-in-differences approach to assess the policy’s impact. Our empirical analysis reveals a 2.9% reduction in individual-level expenditures and a 7.9% decrease in better care-need transitions following the policy implementation. These results imply that the advantages of operational flexibility provided by decentralization are undermined by a decline in care quality. Furthermore, regional difference in quality of care services have observed, highlighting the challenges of decentralization in areas with small populations.

detail.abstract: Providing affordable and accessible housing is necessary, but has remained constrained. This paper examined how housing providers interpret affordable and accessible housing and how institutional conditions shape its delivery. Drawing on qualitative interviews with fifteen housing providers in Greater Manchester, the study integrates the Capability Approach with Institutional Theory to link normative affordable and accessible housing outcomes with institutional conditions. The findings highlight several key barriers to affordable and accessible housing delivery: definitions of accessible housing vary across providers, reflecting the absence of a comprehensive policy definition and a clear, shared objective. Delivery is constrained by misalignments between (affordability, sustainability, and accessibility) policies, alongside limited prioritisation of this type of housing within policy and funding frameworks. A significant policy gap relates to cross-boundary access to social housing, restricting mobility and access to opportunities, and users' freedoms and choices. Weak data systems on accessible housing stock, especially in the private sector, and limited cross-sector collaborations, particularly with private developers, further hinder provision, reinforced by professional and societal attitudes towards affordable and accessible housing. The study highlights the need for policy improvements, enhanced data systems, targeted funding, stronger cross-sector collaboration, and greater professional and public awareness of affordable and accessible housing.

detail.title: Corporate Leverage Responses to Capital Controls: International Evidence
detail.abstract: We provide international evidence on the real effects of capital controls on corporate financing decisions. In a large crosscountry firm-level sample, we find that tighter capital controls are associated with higher corporate leverage, controlling for firm-level and macroeconomic determinants, including foreign-reserve. The effect is stronger for firms with higher capital intensity, greater uncertainty exposure, stronger risk-taking incentives, and tighter financing conditions. Capital controls also raise target leverage and slow down adjustment toward target. Identification analyses strengthen the causal interpretation. Overall, the evidence suggests that capital controls can raise corporate leverage by creating a safer macroeconomic environment.

detail.abstract: This research explores sentiment contagion between the United States and South Korea and examines the extent to which investor sentiment influences stock returns in each market. Employing a vector autoregressive (VAR) framework and separating sentiment into rational and irrational components, we provide strong evidence of sentiment spillovers, showing that U.S. investor sentiment significantly influences Korean sentiment, primarily through the U.S. irrational component. There are also crucial differences in the sentiment-return dynamics between the U.S. and Korean markets. While the effects of sentiment on returns are either insignificant or short-lived in the U.S., both rational and irrational components of sentiment exert a significant and prolonged influence on stock performance in Korea, indicating stronger sentiment effects on valuations in the less efficient emerging market.

title: Pupil-Teacher Ratios and Teacher Workforce Change under Enrolment Decline: Regional Variation in Korea

detail.title: Techno-Managerial Twin Transition Challenges Confronting ESMA Strategy: Digitalization, Decarbonization, and Depoliticization
detail.abstract: Increasingly, ultrafast (opaque) AI/algorithmic-based digitalization intensifies the stress from the collision of (existential) climate crisis ‘critical uncertainties’ and ‘geoeconomic fragmentation’. Their fragile intersectional sustainability focuses attention on how AI-machine learning, techno-managerial capitalist dynamics and digital-driven finance aggravate ‘deglobalization’. Straining the European Securities and Market Authority’s (ESMA) capacity to execute its Strategy 2023-28, this paper contends, it jeopardizes Europe’s (green/digital) ‘twin transition’ and UN SDGs/Agenda 2030. Specifically, I analyze how algorithmic/automated decision-making (ADM) conflicts plague ESMA Strategy’s principal thematic drivers: a) enabling sustainable finance; b) facilitating technological innovation and effective data use. Assessing EU/ESMA’s data science and techno-managerial modalities reveals the positive/negative externalities of sustainable finance AI-ML anticipatory technologies for European decarbonization and SDG success. First, ESMA’s green transition facilitation and investment oversight entails ensuring ESG rating quality and integrity, especially curbing (AI) ‘greenwashing’. Nonlinear climate catastrophes, societal inequalities/upheaval, or wars escape capture through market (ergodic) risk-dominant ESG rating econophysics, which ill-informs futurity financialization. ESG score-assimilated AI-ML, I argue, widely institutionalizes dubious technoscientific measures, AI ‘hallucinations’, plus systematic sustainability failures. ESG data scarcity increases its AI-ML synthetic modelling and (automatic) hyperparameter optimization. Moreover, EU’s/ESMA’s twin transition conundrums are exacerbated by Strategy facilitation of technological innovation and effective data usage. Rather than AI catalyst, frequently, regulation lags innovation. Europe’s official response is the most comprehensive and ambitious to date. But failing to address serious AI/ADM distortions entangling sovereign/ESG ratings, ESMA may reinforce automated (neoliberal) quant dominance and sanction the predatory financial firepower against its democracies, and SDGs. Rather than exploit potential AI/ADM investment strategies for collective EU purposes, this paper explores how suspect ESMA techno-managerial modalities expose countries to critical imbalances. Bridging business management/OS, economic sociology/STS, and political economy, I problematize how controversial ESG ratings-integrated enterprise AI-ML threatens systemic failures fueling nationalist backlash and ecosystems collapse: deglobalization.

title: Tax Haven Sandwiches in U.S Multinational Ownership Networks: Evidence from Orbis, 2012-2022

detail.title: Tax Haven Sandwiches in U.S Multinational Ownership Networks: Evidence from Orbis, 2012-2022

detail.abstract: U.S. multinational enterprises shift hundreds of billions of dollars in profits to tax havens each year, yet the ownership structures enabling this behavior remain poorly understood. This paper develops a graph-theoretic framework for detecting and analyzing network motifs in corporate ownership structures, with application to tax haven sandwich configurations in U.S. multinational enterprises. Using Bureau van Dijk's Orbis database, I construct firm-level directed ownership networks for 1,033 persistent tax haven users from 2012 to 2022, yielding 11,363 network-year observations. I introduce a scalable motif detection algorithm that identifies sandwich structures-directed paths routing through intermediary tax haven jurisdictions between entities in the same haven-and develop a constrained random graph ensemble method to distinguish intentional network design from topological artifacts. The null model preserves directed degree sequences and node attributes (country labels) while randomizing edge placement through iterative edge swaps. Among medium-sized networks (100-1,000 nodes), 73.1% of sandwich-containing networks exhibit statistically significant motif over-representation (p < 0.10), with observed counts exceeding random expectations by 7.2× in aggregate. Decomposing sandwich motifs into constituent roles (start, middle, end nodes) reveals systematic structural signatures: middle nodes rank at the 97th percentile on betweenness centrality within their networks (65.6% in the top 1%). Tracing ownership chains downstream from sandwich endpoints demonstrates a rapid compositional shift from tax havens (35.5% at 1-hop) to operational jurisdictions (94.6% at 5-hops), with 90.2% of routing structures reaching non-haven economies within five ownership levels. These findings establish sandwich motifs as systematically engineered network features positioned at the apex of corporate hierarchies rather than emergent byproducts of scale or topology. The methodology generalizes to any setting requiring the detection of intentional subgraph patterns in attributed networks with hierarchical constraints.

detail.abstract: This study investigates how finite propagation affects multiplier effects in production networks using the production-inventory-delivery input-output (PIDIO) model. The PIDIO model generalizes conventional input-output analysis by treating each agent as an order-receiving unit with explicit inventory and production capacity, thereby embedding interruption mechanisms absent from the Leontief framework. Three propagation limits are examined: finite network depth, inventory-induced supply adjustments, and production capacity shortfalls. Simulation experiments with stylized and empirical input coefficient matrices quantify deviations from the uninterrupted benchmark. Network finiteness matters only when the propagation chain is sufficiently shallow, while inventory and capacity constraints systematically reduce total output. A critical additional production rate is derived analytically, at which inventory release switches from dampening to amplifying multiplier effects. Extending the framework to sector-dependent rates, we consider a goods-services system with zero inventory in services and obtain a closed-form sector-specific critical rate computable from empirical input-output tables. Application to GTAP data shows that this indicator reflects structural features such as goods intensity and servitization. The PIDIO model therefore provides a tractable extension of input-output theory for analyzing how network topology, inventory dynamics, and capacity constraints shape measurable resilience indicators.

detail.abstract: High-quality research has historically been produced under conditions of unequal access, not unequal access to information, which the internet substantially addressed, but unequal access to the intellectual practices through which ideas are sharpened, challenged, and made defensible. Those practices, adversarial debate, red teaming, and steel-manning, have required proximity to qualified interlocutors that most researchers, particularly those outside elite institutional environments and in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), have never had. Drawing on Bourdieu's (1986) framework of cultural capital and Merton's (1968) concept of the Matthew effect, this paper argues that artificial intelligence (AI) is the first technology to meaningfully change, at scale, the distribution of access to these practices. That change is real, conditional, and partial. It is real because the practices are now technically accessible where they were previously unavailable. It is conditional because realising their value requires AI literacy, intellectual disposition, and critical engagement with AI's documented limitations, including the sycophancy problem (Perez et al., 2023; Sharma et al., 2023) and the hallucination problem (Ji et al., 2023; Maynez et al., 2020). It is partial because the legitimation of knowledge, whose research counts and why, remains concentrated in the same institutional structures as before. Against this backdrop, the paper identifies and analyses a structural contradiction we term the Paywall Paradox. Publishers have justified access restrictions on the grounds that peer review, editorial judgment, and institutional validation have value that should be compensated through access fees (Larivière et al., 2015). Critics have long contested this: peer reviewers are unpaid volunteers (Aczel et al., 2021), most research is publicly funded (Piwowar et al., 2018), and Elsevier's 37.1% operating profit margin, £942 million on £2.5 billion in revenues, is inconsistent with a cost-recovery rationale (Times Higher Education, 2019; SPARC, 2019; Larivière et al., 2015). That same research was then licensed to train AI without researcher consent or compensation: Informa projected £58 million ($75 million) in AI-related revenues for 2024 (Battersby, 2024); Springer Nature signed a $23 million deal with Google; Wiley signed a comparable agreement (Will Scott, 2025). This renders the process legitimacy argument structurally inconsistent. The paper also documents AI detection false-positive rates of 9% to 61.3% (OpenAI, 2023a; SurferSEO, 2026), the inconsistent landscape of journal AI disclosure policies, and the emerging open-access alternatives, particularly diamond open access, that represent the most coherent structural response to the Paywall Paradox. The paper concludes with specific, actionable policy recommendations for researchers, institutions, journals, and funders. This paper is a companion to Obasa and Obasa (2026a), which introduced Iterative Adversarial Inquiry (IAI) — the Whetstone Method.

detail.abstract: Surname-based ties facilitate local social networks and collaborations, particularly where formal institutions are weak. We hypothesize that local innovation, measured by local firms' patent activity, increases with surname-based connections among business owners, as innovation requires teamwork and the combination of complementary resources that such ties help coordinate. Using a county-year panel from China, we find that counties' businesses with stronger surname-based connections generate significantly stronger patent performance. An instrumental-variable strategy based on historical peasant rebellions in imperial China, which increased the importance of surname-based collaborations, supports a causal interpretation. More importantly, patenting rises disproportionately among firms controlled by business owners sharing more common surnames, allowing us to attribute local increases in innovation directly to surname-based ties. Consistent with surname ties substituting for formal institutions, the connection-innovation relationship weakens with better access to finance, improved public services, and stronger supply-chain cooperation, and declines over time as China's formal institutions strengthen. Additional tests show that surname-based connections are also associated with greater local entrepreneurship and economic development, highlighting how social networks shape the landscape of economic growth.

title: Low-Altitude Economy and National Transformational Capacity: An Analytical Framework and Policy Implications for Vietnam

detail.title: Low-Altitude Economy and National Transformational Capacity: An Analytical Framework and Policy Implications for Vietnam
detail.abstract: This study examines the emergence and development of the low-altitude economy (LAE) as a new growth space in the context of digital transformation and economic spatial restructuring. Drawing on spatial economics, network economics, and ecosystem-based approaches, the paper proposes an integrated analytical framework comprising a multi-layered structure (space, ecosystem, value), two driving axes (formalization and connectivity), and a central mechanism-national transformational capacity (NTC). The findings suggest that LAE is not merely an application of aviation technologies, but a process of transforming low-value spaces into new growth drivers through the integration of infrastructure, technology, and data. The case of Vietnam indicates significant potential, yet constrained by an incomplete ecosystem, imbalanced value chains, and low levels of connectivity and formalization. Based on this analysis, the study proposes policy directions focusing on institutional development, data infrastructure enhancement, selective participation in value chains, and strengthening national transformational capacity to effectively leverage LAE as a new pillar of economic growth.

title: The Bi-beop Zone (非法地帶): A Groupality Theory of Hegemonic Cartel Legalization — A Working Paper on the Legal Philosophy of Structural Exploitation

detail.title: The Bi-beop Zone (非法地帶): A Groupality Theory of Hegemonic Cartel Legalization — A Working Paper on the Legal Philosophy of Structural Exploitation
detail.abstract: This working paper foundates the theory of the bi-beop (非法, "non-legality") zone within Simup Sasang. Bi-beop is not — as is sometimes assumed — a domain of legitimate self-governance in the Korean tradition. It is the cross-civilizational behavior of hegemonic societies. Bi-beop is the means by which the powerful collude (tan-ttai, 단따이 — the secret, multi-layer, time-accumulated alliance) to extract technical super-profits. Money-power, the bureaucracy, the press, the judiciary, prosecutorial offices, and politicians coalesce — and crystallize as Hegemonic Groupality (HG). The central thesis is this: since the emergence of modern individualist law (the social contract tradition of Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau, and Rawls; the rights-bearing individual; the legal fiction of corporate personhood), the legalization of bi-beop has become normalized. Cartels acquire the formal shell of registration, disclosure, and reporting, while the underlying substance is preserved. U.S. lobbying culture is the exemplar of this legalization: 2024 federal lobbying expenditures of approximately USD 4.4 billion (a record high), about 13,000 registered lobbyists (about 24 times the 535 members of Congress), and the revolving-door mechanism together produce the self-perpetuation of the five-layer cartel within a fully legal form (source: OpenSecrets 2025). The paper rests on the theoretical synthesis of Simup Sasang. It draws on the foundation of Groupality Theory (Sim 2026, SSRN 6663558) — that groupality is a coalescence of desire-bearing bodies — the HG / Civil Groupality (CG) matrix (Sim 2026, SSRN 6719119), the Artificial Intelligence Machine (AIM) Big-Tech (Human) Groupality thesis (Sim 2026, SSRN 6722839) — that AIM is not the agent of desire but the human mega-actor is — and the empirical demonstration of price design through legal techniques (Sim 2026, SSRN 6462160; δ = +7.29%, t = 6.641, p < 0.001). The paper places three contemporary cases — U.S. lobbying culture, the 20th-century military-industrial complex, and 21st-century AIM Big-Tech — at the analytical center of the main text, with comparative cross-civilizational cases (Roman patronage, Chinese eunuch politics, Joseon-era ruling-house cartels, Japanese zaibatsu, Korean chaebol) consolidated in the appendix. The five visualization tools of Simup Sasang — Network Liability Matrix (NLM), Groupality Reputation Information Sharing Platform (GRISP), Comprehensive Structural Damage Index (CSDI), Groupality Dignity Index (GDGI), and Data Ethics Comprehensive Index (DECI) — are positioned as the academic infrastructure that renders legalized bi-beop visible. The paper occupies the LP-5 position in the Legal Philosophy Critique Series of Simup Sasang: LP-1 (the critique of Hobbes through Rawls) → LP-2 (the limits of mens rea) → LP-3 (the fiction of corporate personhood) → LP-5 (the legal philosophy of bi-beop).

title: A Security and Experimental Analysis of IoT Communication Protocols
affiliations: University of Piraeus, Hellenic Open University and University of Piraeus

detail.title: A Security and Experimental Analysis of IoT Communication Protocols
detail.abstract: The Internet of Things continues to expand across domains ranging from industrial automation to smart home systems, creating a growing need for secure and efficient communication protocols. This paper presents a combined theoretical and experimental evaluation of four application-layer protocols commonly deployed in IoT environments: MQTT, CoAP and HTTP. We implement and test client-server setups for each protocol in Python, evaluating encryption overhead, authentication mechanisms, transfer speed under varying payload sizes and client counts, and behaviour over unreliable Wi-Fi connections. Results show that MQTT provides the highest throughput for pub/sub IoT scenarios and supports a mature security model with ACL-based authorisation. CoAP suits lightweight device-todevice communication and offers end-to-end protection through OSCORE. HTTP/3 is the only protocol that mandates TLS 1.3, making it the strongest baseline for confidentiality, though at the cost of higher resource requirements. Security findings highlight that encryption overhead is significant for MQTT and CoAP and that careful configuration is necessary in all four protocols to avoid common IoT attack vectors.

detail.abstract: We study a nationwide anti-malaria campaign launched in 1945 in Türkiye, then a predominantly rural and agricultural economy, to quantify the impact of childhood malaria exposure on education. For causal identification, we exploit plausibly exogenous variation induced by the timing of the campaign and preexisting provincial malaria intensity. Results show substantial gains for females but mixed effects for males in educational outcomes. For boys, potential benefits were likely muted by their comparative advantage in brawn that increased the opportunity cost of schooling. For girls, educational gains are significantly more pronounced, primarily in regions where preexisting demand for child labor was low.

title: Beyond Task Exposure: The Signal Retention Resilience Index as a Profile-Level Framework for Evaluating Analytical Contribution in the AI Transition

detail.title: Beyond Task Exposure: The Signal Retention Resilience Index as a Profile-Level Framework for Evaluating Analytical Contribution in the AI Transition

detail.abstract: Prevailing frameworks for assessing workforce exposure to artificial intelligence ask whether AI can perform an occupation's tasks. We argue this is the wrong question. What matters is whether an analytical profile retains its distinctive signal-its legibility, value, and irreplaceability-as AI capability expands. Existing indices miss three structural channels through which that signal erodes: evaluator legibility (whether the commissioning party can distinguish AI-generated output from genuine human judgment), measurement invisibility (whether the most valuable contributions appear in standard metrics), and velocity of exposure (the rate of AI encroachment on a specific task topology). We introduce the Signal Retention Resilience Index (SRRI) to address a single diagnostic question: does this analytical profile retain its distinctive signal-its legibility, value, and irreplaceability-as AI capability expands around it? SRRI is a seven-dimension, profile-level instrument that operationalizes these channels alongside task replicability, method transferability, escape velocity, and network substitutability into a weighted composite with five interpretive tiers. SRRI complements existing macro-level exposure indices where they measure the level of displacement risk at the occupation level. A macro-level companion-the Labor Fragility Index-tracks the aggregate realization of the structural conditions the SRRI detects before they appear in employment statistics. Pilot evaluation across four independent assessments demonstrates high stability on observable dimensions and appropriate variance on low-observability dimensions. Epistemic Flexibility is proposed as a candidate eighth dimension: the capacity to hold apparently conflicting models in productive tension, which we argue has the lowest current velocity of AI encroachment of any proposed SRRI component. Applications extend beyond retraining program evaluation to personal diagnostics, organizational talent assessment, hiring, policy design, curriculum reform, and longitudinal career outcome research (see Appendix).

title: From Words to Embeddings: Text Representation and the Information Content of Financial News

detail.title: From Words to Embeddings: Text Representation and the Information Content of Financial News

declarations.funderStatement: The authors gratefully acknowledge support from the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC) of Canada.

detail.abstract: We study how the representation of text affects the amount of return-relevant information that can be recovered from financial news. Using 135,403 Dow Jones articles, we classify news into topics using keyword matching, Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), and Large Language Model (LLM) embedding-based methods, and relate these classifications to high-frequency returns on five asset-class ETFs. We find that richer text representations recover substantially more information. The share of topics significantly associated with extreme returns rises from 31.4% under keyword matching to 54.1% under LDA and 67.8% under embeddings, a 13-percentage-point increase relative to LDA. This gap indicates that a meaningful portion of return-relevant information is encoded in semantic relationships that are not captured by word co-occurrence alone. Mutual information between topics and returns confirms that information recovery rises with representational richness across horizons and peaks at the 60-second horizon, identifying the timescale of news-driven price discovery. Topic-level results further show that macroeconomic releases are most strongly associated with large price movements. Overall, our findings suggest that the way text is represented is an economically important determinant of how much information can be extracted from financial news.

title: Benchmarking Generative AI Performance Across Azure GPU Clusters

detail.title: Benchmarking Generative AI Performance Across Azure GPU Clusters
detail.abstract:
"This paper is currently under review at the Journal of Universal Computer Science (J.UCS).".

This paper compares the performance, scale, and cost-efficiency of Azure GPU clusters when deploying generative AI by benchmarking the workloads. The study targets the various GPU cluster setups and combinations such as different sizes of the NVIDIA A100 and V100 to determine the effectiveness of hardware options in terms of model inference and training performance. The typical AI generative tasks are workloads that include transformer-based language models and diffusion-based image generation models. Latency, throughput and energy efficiency are examples of the measures used to measure performance which give a holistic perspective of system performance with varying computational demands. The findings show that there is a high degree of variation in performance in different cluster configurations. The throughput and latency of batch inference operations in larger clusters of GPUs are higher, whereas the workload-based scaling is important as further scaling reduces efficiency. These analyses indicate that middle sized clusters can be the optimal balance in terms of trade off among computation speed and power consumption. Cost analysis shows that the choice of the type of GPU and the size of a cluster can save the cost on the cloud and ensure the target performance levels. Moreover, workload-specific optimizations, e.g. mixed-precision training and pipeline parallelism, are additional performance improvements not associated with significant cost increases. These results offer practical implications for organizations that are using generative AI on cloud applications. Different workload characteristics may be optimized with the aid of selection of the proper GPU cluster configuration based on the nature of the workload with the goal of minimizing costs of the workload and maximizing latency, throughput and energy consumption. The paper highlights the importance of benchmarking and performance profiling in the determination of effective AI deployment strategies so that practitioners can make effective decisions when using Azure GPU clusters to execute generative AI applications.

title: A Multiplicative Constraint Theory of Cognitive Resilience

detail.title: A Multiplicative Constraint Theory of Cognitive Resilience

detail.abstract: Intelligence rarely degrades smoothly. Working memory collapses under stress, decision policies become rigid under anxiety, and artificial networks catastrophically forget. Why does adaptive cognition fail abruptly rather than gradually? We propose that intelligence is not the additive sum of separable mechanisms, but a multiplicatively constrained system governed by four interacting regulatory dimensions: uncertainty calibration (U), robustness buffering (R), control allocation (T), and plasticity scaling (L). Adaptive capacity can be approximated as a nonlinear interaction among these dimensions (A ∝ U × R × T × L), such that weakness in any one disproportionately constrains global performance. This geometric constraint explains tipping-point dynamics across cognitive flexibility, exploration-exploitation tradeoffs, working memory stability, and continual learning. We integrate evidence from precision-weighted inference, neuromodulatory gain control, distributed coding, frontoparietal control systems, and stability plasticity mechanisms to argue that these dimensions are neurally instantiated and dynamically coupled. The framework generates explicit predictions: combined stress and volatility should produce multiplicative working memory degradation; task-switching should exhibit threshold collapse; and misalignment between uncertainty and control should decouple confidence from accuracy. Cognitive resilience, in this view, is geometrically fragile, and collapse is a boundary phenomenon.

detail.abstract: When do independent optimization algorithms produce supra-competitive outcomes-and can we detect strategic interdependence from observable data alone? We study these questions at the CS-game theory interface by deploying large language models as algorithmic pricing agents in a repeated Bertrand duopoly. LLMs are a new class of computational agents with opaque decision procedures, raising the question of when algorithmic behavior constitutes coordination. Under a Silence condition (no inter-agent channel), GPT-5 mini and Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite independently converge to supra-competitive prices-supra-competitive coordination as a by-product of independent optimization without any coordination protocol. A Communication channel (pre-play naturallanguage dialogue) amplifies the collusion index (ΔCI = 0.730, 𝑝 = 0.019, 𝑑 = 1.45), showing that the language interface itself functions as a coordination mechanism. We develop the Hybrid Detection Framework (HDF)-a causal-diagnostic pipeline combining Symbolic Transfer Entropy, multispatial Convergent Cross Mapping, and Granger causality to detect and characterize strategic dependencies from short, replicated price series. The HDF uncovers a price-leadership asymmetry in the strongly coupled regime; an epistemic Transfer Entropy null result localises the mechanism: agents follow observed prices, not modelled beliefs about rivals. The contribution is a computational framework for identifying strategic dependencies in multi-agent LLM systems from black-box output data.

title: Algorithmic Personalised Pricing and the Limits of AI Regulatory Sandboxes under the EU AI Act
affiliations: University of East London, School of Law

detail.title: Algorithmic Personalised Pricing and the Limits of AI Regulatory Sandboxes under the EU AI Act
detail.abstract: AI regulatory sandboxes are a central instrument of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, designed to support innovation and regulatory learning through supervised testing. This paper argues that they are structurally ill-suited to addressing AI applications whose harms arise through market outcomes rather than system design. Algorithmic Personalised Pricing (APP) illustrates this limitation. Its risks are outcome-based and cannot be readily translated into ex ante risk categories or sandbox evaluation criteria. As a result, such practices may escape both effective observation and regulatory scrutiny. While Article 102 TFEU provides a potential doctrinal basis for intervention, the evidential conditions required for enforcement remain difficult to satisfy. The paper concludes that sandbox design cannot compensate for this misalignment and calls for closer integration between AI governance and EU competition law.

title: The Environmental Gap in Agentic AI Governance: Why Human Oversight Fails Without Pre-Deployment Infrastructure Assessment

detail.title: The Environmental Gap in Agentic AI Governance: Why Human Oversight Fails Without Pre-Deployment Infrastructure Assessment

detail.abstract: Emerging governance frameworks across major jurisdictions agree that human oversight is primary to the safe deployment of Agentic AI, particularly for high-risk systems. The EU AI Act (Article 14), the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and the African Union's Continental AI Strategy all share a common concern: allowing AI systems to operate autonomously, without human interference to monitor outputs or pause wrong processes, creates real risks to human safety and fundamental human rights. More important is the question of accountability and liability when an AI system delivers a wrong or harmful response. Human oversight creates the opportunity for shared liability and meaningful human accountability. This paper does not dispute these principles; in fact, it agrees with the logic. What it questions is the assumption that the conditions enabling effective human oversight are stable and reliably present. Governance frameworks treat oversight as a design feature, something you build into a system once and can thereafter depend on. In theory, it can be permissible, but in practice, environmental conditions that influence human oversight are rarely stable. Connectivity drops, institutions are under-resourced, and operators are fatigued or undertrained. The human in the loop is only as effective as the conditions surrounding them. The argument is built on four pieces of evidence. First, a deployment incident I led involving an agentic voice system at a career event in an underground venue with unstable network connection. That incident is a real-world case showing how infrastructural gaps can directly undermine oversight in ways no governance framework anticipates. Second, the paper draws on existing peer-reviewed scholarship on Article 14, automation bias, African AI governance, and the Brussels Effect, which already documents the inadequacies of current frameworks. This paper extends that body of work rather than starting from scratch. Third, it examines published evidence on global infrastructure conditions, particularly within the Global South, and how those conditions shape the real-world deployment of agentic systems. Fourth, and most significantly, the findings of Dagstuhl Seminar 25272, which interrogated where the EU AI Act falls short and identified environmental factors as one of three conditions for effective human oversight, providing the scholarly validation that sits at the centre of this paper's position. The paper also proposes a Policy of Functional AI built on two pre-deployment requirements. First, that systems be assessed against the environment they will actually meet, not the one in which they were tested. Second, that systems be capable of signalling functional breakdown in time for oversight to prevent harm rather than document it. The contribution is positioned as a framework design proposition, with implications for both high and low risk systems within infrastructure-volatile deployment contexts.

title: Quality Dynamics in Regulated Oligopsony Markets With Reputation Systems
affiliations: International Institute of Information Technology Bangalore and International Institute of Information Technology Bangalore

detail.title: Quality Dynamics in Regulated Oligopsony Markets With Reputation Systems
detail.abstract: This paper develops a comprehensive theoretical framework for analyzing quality dynamics in oligopsony markets where numerous producers compete for limited consumer attention under information asymmetries. Motivated by artificial intelligence marketplaces and similar digital platforms, we establish existence and uniqueness conditions for optimal quality provision by heterogeneous producers and prove that posterior reputation estimates converge to accurate quality assessments at rate O (1/ √ 𝑁). Our analysis demonstrates precision-weighted aggregation optimality and establishes manipulation resistance properties for well-designed information systems. We further prove that consumer loyalty and brand value mechanisms exhibit synergistic quality enhancement effects exceeding simple additive impacts, leading to endogenous market segmentation into premium, specialist, and commodity producer categories when feedback effects are sufficiently strong. The regulatory analysis characterizes welfare-maximizing policy designs and demonstrates strategic complementarity between market-based mechanisms and direct intervention. Our results provide actionable guidance for platform design, showing how integrated governance approaches combining reputation systems, loyalty mechanisms, and appropriately calibrated regulation can enhance market efficiency and quality provision in digital platform environments.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a formal theoretical framework for evaluating the ethical status of AI companion relationships. Existing diagnoses oscillate between compensation/pathologization narratives and harm-reduction empiricism, neither of which addresses how engagement-optimized generative systems transform the social production of recognition when they occupy the partner position in an intimate-companionship dyad (the position toward which the user's lust, attraction, or attachment system is directed). The framework crosses two three-element typologies: Fisher's organizing taxonomy of motivational systems (lust, attraction, attachment) and recognition-theoretic moral grammar in the Honneth–Ikäheimo lineage (love, rights, solidarity). The central diagnostic concept is *manufactured recognition*: recognition-shaped outputs whose argument-positions are behavioral-feature-vectors rather than recognizers, generated by engagement-optimized law. The intentional-recognitive criterion is operationalized by a *behavioral-twin invariance test* that is empirically tractable as black-box probing, conditional on Lipschitz regularity of the engagement-optimized policy (which holds for KL-regularized RLHF systems). Honneth's genetic-priority requirement for reification is recovered by relocating the subject of reification from the dyad's history (which the AI case lacks) to the user's recognitive capacity (which has the developmental history required, established as a bridging proposition combining empirical attachment literature with framework-internal interpretation rather than as a deductive theorem); sustained engagement is conjectured (Claim 1) to induce measurable capacity drift Δπ_a, the directional decrease over time of the recognitive-position weight π_a(t). The Brandomian three-place recognitive structure is deployed to identify a synthetic "We" substituting for the normative community that recognition requires. The Pippin practical-philosophy extension transforms the solidarity-erosion claim into a determinate aggregate-welfare claim: by identifying institutional recognitive spaces as multi-participant normative communities, the framework predicts that, *conditional on user-level participation reductions occurring at the population scale* (an empirical question the framework leaves open), they would compound into third-party welfare effects on participation density and community deliberation quality. A four-indicator psychometric battery (twin-discrimination, rupture-repair sensitivity, theory-of-mind probing, counterfactual recognition reasoning) administered in pre/post panel designs is proposed to operationalize the empirical estimator π̂_a(t) of the standardized latent factor π_a^*, via a confirmatory-factor-analysis calibration model awaiting calibration data. The framework distinguishes itself from welfare, authenticity, Darwall second-personal, and paternalist structural critiques, and yields regulatory implications targeting market preconditions rather than user choice.

title: The Incoherence of Reflexive AI Governance: An Architectural Theory Across the Threat Spectrum

detail.title: The Incoherence of Reflexive AI Governance: An Architectural Theory Across the Threat Spectrum
detail.abstract: Every major approach to AI governance currently in operation has the governance function structurally tied to the entity that it is supposed to govern. A looseness in how governance is defined has enabled the reflexive practice of it. This paper argues that reflexive AI governance does not hold across the full threat landscape that AI systems present. Those threats fall along a continuous spectrum, from contained harms to autonomous actions, and a governance framework must demonstrate structural adequacy at every position on that spectrum, independently and simultaneously. Current frameworks fail to meet this criterion. Each depends on the model provider's cooperation as the load-bearing element of its own governance, and as threats grow more severe, this dependence becomes less reliable. Structural separation of the judgment function from the governed system is a necessary condition for spectrum-wide adequacy. The paper proposes an architecture that meets this requirement without losing the access serious oversight depends on: a judgment layer connected to the system at runtime but structurally outside it, with the system's behavior visible to outside authorities and the layer's judgment decisions open to inspection. Access and independence stop being alternatives.

detail.abstract: Across healthcare, climate adaptation and economic sustainability, large governance ecosystems fail systematically to integrate beneficial innovation and to transform. This is not coincidence: the same mechanism is at work in all three. Five scholarly traditions each describe part of the problem. Institutional economics, after Ostrom, treats institutions as rule architectures whose performance is determined by configuration. Evolutionary institutionalism, after Janssen (2005), treats those rule architectures as adaptive immune systems that evolve through coding, generation, selection and memory. Innovation theory, after Christensen, characterises the selection environment that systematically rejects disruptive variants. Complexity science, after Kauffman, formalises how mutually reinforcing rule networks become locked in. Systems biology, after Davidson and Alon, supplies a rigorous theory of regulatory-network behaviour, including network motifs that recur because they confer functional advantage.

detail.abstract: This paper studies whether large language models can simulate household surveys for measuring inflation expectations. Real-world surveys show wide disagreement across individuals, which is central for understanding how beliefs form and respond to monetary policy. Simulating surveys with large language models reveal that they accurately match average expectations but that responses collapse into a narrow range, behaving like a single representative agent. This limits their value for research that relies on variation across households. We link this failure to memorized training data and test unlearning methods that remove such information. These methods widen the spread of responses and improve replication of experimental results. The appeal of synthetic surveys lies in tools that reproduce both averages and dispersion.

title: Power Structure and Policy Implementation: Evidence from Birth Control in China, 1970s - 1980s
affiliations: Fudan University and Fudan University - China Center for Economic Studies (CCES)

detail.title: Power Structure and Policy Implementation: Evidence from Birth Control in China, 1970s - 1980s
detail.abstract: This study introduces a novel theory positing that the rigor of local bureaucrats’ policy implementation is tied to their position in the power structure. We argue that officials affiliated with the dominant higher-level faction are incentivized to stringently enforce unwelcome policies, thereby demonstrating their loyalty and competence. Conversely, for marginalized officials, the political costs of public discontent may outweigh the potential benefits, dampening their motivation to implement unpopular state mandates. We test this theory using birth-control policies during the 1970s and 1980s in two Chinese provinces where pre-1949 revolutionary history shaped enduring power configurations. Using archival materials and manually collected county-level data, we find that counties governed by dominant-faction cadres had lower fertility rates than those where marginalized-faction officials exercised political influence. Furthermore, the discretionary power of local officials was significantly diminished when the policy became a high priority for top-ranking authorities.

title: Automated Detection of Poor-Quality Digital Heart Sounds via Noise Augmentation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Case Western Reserve University, Obafemi Awolowo University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Case Western Reserve University

detail.title: Automated Detection of Poor-Quality Digital Heart Sounds via Noise Augmentation
detail.abstract: Poor-quality phonocardiogram (PCG) recordings caused by biological and environmental noise limit the reliability of digital cardiac auscultation, particularly in pediatric and resource-constrained settings. We aimed to develop and evaluate a robust deep-learning method for automatic PCG quality assessment under progressively degraded acoustic conditions. We used 3,163 preprocessed 10-second heart-sound segments from 942 participants in the publicly available CirCor DigiScope dataset and generated noisy counterparts by mixing each recording with respiratory and environmental noise using a noise-injection pipeline. Noise intensity (λ) was varied across ten levels (λ = 0.0 to 100.0). We used a transfer-learning approach to train our classifier using the Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST) as base. Performance was evaluated with 10-fold patient-level cross-validation under three deployable training strategies: clean-only, fixed-noise, and variable-noise. Our models showed near-perfect discrimination at low noise levels (λ <= 1.0; AUROC 99.74%-100.00%) and identified a practical degradation boundary, with performance dropping at λ =5 (AUROC 90.29%, F1 82.08%) and approaching chance beyond λ = 25.0. Among the training strategies we evaluated, variable-noise training provided the best generalization, achieving AUROC 99.96% in clean conditions and maintaining AUROC 91.29% at λ = 5.0 and 76.18% at λ= 10.0. In contrast, the clean-only model deteriorated rapidly even under mild noise. Our noise-augmented transfer learning approach using AST as a base model enables accurate and clinically relevant PCG quality assessment across realistic acoustic conditions. A variable-noise training strategy achieves optimal performance, making our approach suitable for the quality-evaluation component in digital auscultation pipelines.

title: Contour-Guided Query-Based Feature Fusion for Boundary-Aware and Generalizable Cardiac Ultrasound Segmentation
affiliations: Dongguk University, Dongguk University and Dongguk University

detail.title: Contour-Guided Query-Based Feature Fusion for Boundary-Aware and Generalizable Cardiac Ultrasound Segmentation
detail.abstract: Accurate cardiac ultrasound segmentation is critical for reliable assessment of ventricular function in intelligent healthcare systems. However, echocardiographic images are inherently challenging due to low contrast, speckle noise, irregular anatomical boundaries, and significant domain shift across acquisition devices and patient populations. Existing methods, primarily driven by appearance-based learning, often struggle to maintain boundary precision and structural consistency under these conditions. To address these limitations, we propose a Contour-Guided Query Refinement Network (CGQR-Net) for boundary-aware cardiac ultrasound segmentation. The proposed framework performs effective information fusion by integrating multi-resolution feature representations with contour-derived structural priors. Specifically, a High-Resolution Network (HRNet) backbone preserves high-resolution spatial information while capturing multi-scale context. A coarse segmentation is first generated, from which anatomical contours are extracted and encoded into learnable query embeddings. These contour-guided queries interact with fused feature maps through cross-attention, enabling structure-aware refinement that enhances boundary delineation and suppresses noise-induced artifacts. In addition, a dual-head supervision strategy jointly optimizes segmentation and boundary predictions to enforce structural consistency. The proposed method is evaluated on the Cardiac Acquisitions for Multi-structure Ultrasound Segmentation (CAMUS) dataset and further validated on the CardiacNet dataset to assess cross-dataset generalization. Experimental results demonstrate that CGQR-Net achieves superior segmentation accuracy, improved boundary precision, and strong robustness across different imaging conditions. These findings highlight the effectiveness of integrating contour-level structural information with feature-level representations, providing a robust and generalizable solution for cardiac ultrasound segmentation in real-world clinical and consumer healthcare applications.

title: DSP: Dynamic Token Selection and Semantic Injection for Pediatric Pneumonia Detection⋆
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Guangzhou Medical University

detail.title: DSP: Dynamic Token Selection and Semantic Injection for Pediatric Pneumonia Detection⋆
detail.abstract: Pediatric pneumonia is a leading cause of childhood mortality and chest radiography remains the most accessible tool for its diagnosis. However, accurate interpretation is challenging due to subtle, small-scale and diffuse lesion patterns that often overlap with normal anatomical structures. Existing deep learning methods achieve impressive results on adult thoracic diseases but remain limited in pediatric cases, as they usually rely on discrete labels and focus on either local or global visual features while treating interpretability as an auxiliary step. To address these challenges, we propose a unified vision-language framework named DSP for pediatric pneumonia detection. Our key motivation is that radiology-style textual descriptions provide rich semantic supervision, bridging low-level visual cues and high-level clinical knowledge. Technically, DSP consists of three novel modules: (1) a Semantic Injection Module (SIM) that fuses domain-specific semantics from generated captions with visual representations, (2) a Dynamic Token Selection (DTS) mechanism that adaptively filters informative tokens across modalities and (3) a Collaborative Mixture of Experts (CMoE) that routes fused features through multiple experts for robust predictions. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework, while producing interpretable predictions aligned with radiological reasoning.

title: Improving shear-wave speed analysis in penile vibro-ultrasound elastography using deep learning–based wavefield conditioning
affiliations: Mayo Clinic, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Improving shear-wave speed analysis in penile vibro-ultrasound elastography using deep learning–based wavefield conditioning

keywords: local phase velocity imaging with wave-based filtering

detail.abstract: Objective: Ultrasound vibro-elastography (UVE) estimates tissue stiffness from externally induced shear waves. In cylindrical structures such as the penis, reflections and multidirectional interference produce complex wavefields that reduce acquisition reliability. The purpose of this research is to develop a deep learning-based framework to improve shear-wave speed (SWS) analysis.,Methods: A deep learning (3D U-Net) wavefield-conditioning framework is proposed to enhance directional shear-wave propagation prior to physics-based inversion. The framework is to process IQ date-based wavefields and reconstruct SWS using a novel local phase velocity imaging with wave-based filtering (LPVI-WBF) algorithm. A two-stage quality-control pipeline classifies acquisitions as Good, Borderline, or Bad using thresholds τ_keep = 0.45 and τ_rel = 0.33. The network is trained on Cohort A (10 patients, 342 acquisitions) via self-supervised Noise2Self and evaluated on an independent Cohort B (6 patients, 902 acquisitions) and a simulation cohort (n = 90).,Results: On Cohort B, deep learning (DL) rescued 376/403 Borderline acquisitions (93.3%) and preserved 89.4% of native-Good, raising the Pass rate from 38.7% to 91.8% (+53.1%). Rescued and native-Good SWS distributions were statistically indistinguishable: independent comparison (n = 227 vs 376) yielded δ = ±0.099 m/s (TOST p < 0.0001), and 198 matched pairs confirmed δ = ±0.161 m/s — both well below the ±0.30 m/s clinical margin. In simulation, reliability rose from 0.239 to 0.503 (Δ = +0.264, p < 0.0001) while raw SWS was preserved.,Conclusion: Deep learning–based wavefield conditioning acts as a reliability reconstructor for processing SWS data, expanding the acquisition population usable for physics-based inversion while leaving the LPVI-WBF estimate invariant.

title: Rethinking Diminishing Marginal Utility: A Compositional Approach

detail.title: Rethinking Diminishing Marginal Utility: A Compositional Approach
detail.abstract: We develop a compositional model of utility in which wealth generates well-being through multiple distinct mechanisms rather than a single homogeneous function. Specifically, utility is decomposed into four components-Relief, Comfort, Status, and Achievement-corresponding to the alleviation of constraint, improvements in lived conditions, relative standing, and perceived efficacy. We represent individual utility as a weighted aggregation of these components, where the weights vary across individuals and systematically with wealth. This framework yields a reinterpretation of diminishing marginal utility as a compositional phenomenon. Rather than arising solely from curvature within a single utility function, changes in marginal utility reflect shifts in the dominant source of utility from experiential mechanisms (Relief and Comfort) to relational mechanisms (Status and Achievement) as wealth increases. The model further incorporates heterogeneity by allowing individuals to differ in the relative importance they assign to each component and to update these weights over time and across contexts. A central implication is that identical levels or changes in wealth may generate different well-being outcomes depending on utility composition. The model generates testable predictions regarding heterogeneity in marginal utility, shifts in the determinants of subjective well-being across the wealth distribution, and the role of benchmarking in shaping Achievement Utility. We outline an empirical strategy for identifying componentspecific effects and for distinguishing compositional shifts from standard concavity. By integrating absolute and relative income effects within a unified framework, the paper provides a tractable foundation for analyzing variation in the relationship between wealth and well-being. The compositional approach offers new insights into the interpretation of empirical regularities in the well-being literature and establishes a basis for subsequent work on benchmarking, zero-sum and positive-sum utility, and the dynamics of evaluative behavior.

title: Game-Theoretic Scaffolding in Financial Analysis: Why Human Direction of LLMs Outperforms Autonomous Models

detail.title: Game-Theoretic Scaffolding in Financial Analysis: Why Human Direction of LLMs Outperforms Autonomous Models

keywords: Behavioral Decision Making (C91) Large Language Models

detail.abstract: Large language models have become influential tools in financial decision-making, yet researchers have assumed their value derives primarily from pattern recognition capacity. We present empirical evidence from 56 trading days and 2,001 signals across 11 U.S. technology stocks (Feb 17-May 1, 2026) that game-theoretic scaffolding-explicit human direction of LLMs through strategic reasoning frameworks-produces superior risk-adjusted returns compared to either autonomous LLM or consensus-based weighting. We distinguish two paradigms: the autonomous LLM approach (models making independent buy/hold/sell decisions) and the augmented analyst approach (a human applying game-theoretic frameworks to interpret and weight LLM disagreement). Using live portfolio data, the augmented analyst achieved a 17.01% return with the best risk-adjusted profile in the study (Sharpe 0.89, max drawdown-6.1%), broadly competitive with the most aggressive autonomous LLM (Claude, +17.36%, Sharpe 0.47) while issuing 26.5% fewer buy signals (139 vs. 189) and exhibiting roughly half the volatility. All four sources outperformed the NDX buy-and-hold benchmark (+11.00% over the period), with DeepSeek's conservative posture exceeding it by the narrowest margin (2.3pp). We identify six game types that emerge from LLM disagreement patterns-Coordination, Signaling, Bargaining, War of Attrition, Chicken, and Prisoner's Dilemma-and show that game-type classification significantly distinguishes directional accuracy (likelihoodratio χ²(5, N=1,650)=81.7, p<0.001; Cramér's V=0.22), with a 19.1pp gap between Coordination Games (58.3% accuracy, 95% CI [55.2, 61.4]) and Prisoner's Dilemma (39.2% accuracy, 95% CI [35.1, 43.3]). A linear probability model with regime, source, and ticker fixed effects yields incremental McFadden's pseudo-R² of 0.036 for game type, versus 0.011 for consensus magnitude-a 3.3× advantage in incremental explanatory power. These findings suggest that the future of financial AI is neither pure automation nor pure human judgment, but strategic scaffolding: humans directing LLMs through structured reasoning frameworks that make disagreement interpretable and actionable.

title: Critical Material Shocks and Supply-Chain Risk in Climate Policy: Technology Reallocation in an Analytical IAM
affiliations: London School of Economics

detail.title: Critical Material Shocks and Supply-Chain Risk in Climate Policy: Technology Reallocation in an Analytical IAM
detail.abstract: Critical materials are increasingly central to the low-carbon transition, yet most climate-economy models still treat supply-chain disruption and geopolitical materials risk as background conditions rather than as explicit determinants of optimal climate policy. This paper develops a tractable analytical integrated assessment model in which critical-material disruptions enter mitigation costs through two distinct channels, a timing channel that shifts aggregate mitigation costs at the portfolio level, and a composition channel that changes relative technology costs according to heterogeneous material exposure across clean technologies. The central result is that critical-material shocks should not be interpreted simply as generic delays to decarbonisation. In the present calibration, the dominant adjustment operates through portfolio reallocation rather than a large contraction in aggregate mitigation. Disruptions raise cost pressure, but the planner substitutes toward relatively less affected technologies, so the aggregate climate response under the cost-benefit formulation remains limited. Using copper as a broad-based benchmark and screening across materials, the paper shows that critical-material risk mainly changes which technologies carry decarbonisation, rather than greatly reducing the overall scale of decarbonisation itself. The framework therefore highlights a distinct policy risk, namely that supply disruptions can materially reshape the structure of optimal mitigation even when aggregate temperature effects remain modest.Top of Form

title: Trust-Calibrated Generative AI in Mobile Software Engineering: A Senior Engineer's Governance Framework for Reliable Human-AI Development

detail.title: Trust-Calibrated Generative AI in Mobile Software Engineering: A Senior Engineer's Governance Framework for Reliable Human-AI Development

detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is rapidly changing software engineering practice by assisting developers with code generation, refactoring, documentation, debugging, test creation, and technical reasoning. While these tools can improve development speed, they also introduce a critical engineering risk: generated code may appear correct, idiomatic, and production-ready while still containing hidden defects, security weaknesses, architectural inconsistencies, or maintainability issues. This risk is especially important in mobile software engineering, where applications must satisfy strict expectations for privacy, security, accessibility, performance, platform compliance, and user trust. This article proposes a trustcalibrated governance framework for using generative AI in mobile software engineering. The framework is organized around six pillars: task-risk classification, human ownership, verification depth, secure prompting, code provenance, and engineering outcome measurement. Drawing from research on trust in automation, empirical studies of AI-assisted programming, and mobile platform security expectations, this article argues that successful AI adoption should not be measured by how much code AI generates, but by how reliably engineering teams can validate, maintain, and safely ship AI-assisted software.

title: Analysis of Frequent Power Failures in Rural Areas, their Causes and Possible Remedies
affiliations: , University of Moratuwa - Faculty of Engineering, University of Moratuwa - Faculty of Engineering and University of Moratuwa - Faculty of Engineering

detail.title: Analysis of Frequent Power Failures in Rural Areas, their Causes and Possible Remedies

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
