detail.abstract: The need to have large-scale enterprise knowledge retrieval with high relevance and low latency is also obliging semantic search systems to deliver on these requirements. This paper explores a scalable semantic search engine which combines retrievalaugmented generation (RAG) with Azure Cognitive Search and Azure OpenAI large language models. The system was evaluated on a corpus of 1.2 million enterprise style documents which were technical manuals, research articles and structured metadata records. The network proposed is a weighted synthesis using generative model and language models along with vector-based retrieval to produce responses to the given context. The experimental comparison of the proposed method and a baseline semantic retrieval system on embedding-based search was carried out. Findings indicate that the RAG-based system increased retrieval accuracy (0.78 to 0.89) and recall accuracy (0.72-0.87) by 17% in F1-score. Experiments on scalability also confirmed that there is consistent response latency when the query load is large, and that average response times are less than 1.05 seconds with datasets of more than two million indexed documents. Such results show that by combining generative AI and enterprise semantic search, it is possible to maximize contextual retrieval accuracy but still have scalable performance in large knowledge repositories.

title: Customer Lifetime Value for Strategic Capital Allocation and Decision Optimization
affiliations: New England College

detail.title: Customer Lifetime Value for Strategic Capital Allocation and Decision Optimization
detail.abstract: Businesses base their customer acquisition and retention choices on short-term investment return measurements which fail to show complete customer value throughout their relationship with the business. The study introduces a machinelearning-based Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) framework which connects predictive analytics with budget-constrained optimization for strategic capital allocation purposes. The proposed method uses CLV prediction together with uncertainty estimation and risk-adjusted valuation to distribute marketing resources among different customer segments while staying within financial limits. The framework evaluation uses a customer-level transactional panel which includes 150,000 customers and 2.5 million transactions over a 24-month observation period. The study evaluates three different allocation methods which include equal-budget allocation and ROI-based allocation and CLV-based allocation. The results demonstrate that CLV-based allocation produces the highest expected profit while also improving customer equity growth and resource efficiency compared to the benchmark policies. The CLV-based policy maintains its effectiveness because it operates better than all other policies during situations which include high churn and increased marketing costs and dwindling demand. The study finds that businesses gain the most from CLV when they use it as a decision-making instrument instead of using it only for forecasting or customer segmentation. The framework establishes a foundation for customer-centric capital allocation through its combination of machine learning and optimization which enables businesses to make investment decisions based on long-term value.

title: After the Blue Ocean How AI Reshapes the Imitation Barriers in Kim and Mauborgne's Framework A conceptual extension of Blue Ocean Strategy (2005) for the AI era

detail.title: After the Blue Ocean How AI Reshapes the Imitation Barriers in Kim and Mauborgne's Framework A conceptual extension of Blue Ocean Strategy (2005) for the AI era

keywords: generative AI JEL Classification M10 (General Business Administration)

detail.abstract: W. Chan Kim and Renée Mauborgne's Blue Ocean Strategy (2005) gave management thought one of its most important reframes of the past quarter century: industry boundaries are not fixed, and firms can create uncontested market space rather than compete for shrinking demand. Central to that reframe is a claim about sustainability. Chapter 9 of the book identifies eight imitation barriers that, the authors argue, typically protect a blue ocean for ten to fifteen years. This paper revisits those barriers under conditions the original framework was not built for. Drawing on three industry cases (generative-AI SaaS, direct-to-consumer beauty, and US commercial airlines), it argues that the eight barriers do not weaken uniformly under AI. In capability-abundant fast-cycle industries, four of the eight collapse outright and two more weaken substantially within roughly twenty-four months. In capability-scarce slow-cycle industries, most still hold. Direct-to-consumer beauty sits between the two, with barriers eroding through channel and content commoditisation rather than capability replication. The paper proposes two additions to the BOS framework: imitation velocity as a named, industryspecific construct, and a short diagnostic that helps a strategist judge which version of BOS applies to their context. The contribution is conceptual; the paper offers no original empirical data and treats the three cases as analytical anchors rather than proof. Empirical validation of imitation velocity is the natural next step.

detail.abstract: The administration of percentage rent-a variable lease structure in which tenant payments are partially determined by gross sales performance-represents one of the most operationally complex and error-prone processes in commercial real estate portfolio management. As retail and commercial lease portfolios increasingly span multiple global regions, the challenges of jurisdictional variation, gross sales definition inconsistency, data fragmentation, multi-currency complexity, vendor-level allocation, and base-rent reconciliation compound in ways that existing enterprise software frameworks have not systematically addressed. This paper employs a Design Science Research (DSR) methodology to derive and propose the Global Lease Compliance Framework (GLCF)-a four-pillar practitioner-grounded framework for enterprise lease compliance at scale. The four pillars-Rules Engine Architecture, Data Governance as Prerequisite, Reconciliation by Design, and Localization Beyond Translation-constitute an artifact designed to address documented failures in global lease administration. The framework is evaluated against existing literature in PropTech, enterprise data governance, and lease accounting standards (FASB ASC 842, IFRS 16) to demonstrate its contribution to real estate technology standardization. Implications for SaaS vendors, corporate occupiers, and the broader PropTech industry are discussed, with future research directions identified.

title: "Myths" on the Benefits of Punitive Sentencing Predict Public Support for the Punishment of Drug Crimes
affiliations: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey - School of Criminal Justice

detail.title: "Myths" on the Benefits of Punitive Sentencing Predict Public Support for the Punishment of Drug Crimes
detail.abstract: Building upon prior work, this experiment with a national sample of U.S. adults (N = 1,547) examines the influence of public beliefs about different “myths” surrounding the potential benefits of harsh drug sentencing on support for punitive sentencing policies for various drug crimes. Results show that increased public support for the use of harsh sentencing strategies for the serious trafficking of serious drugs appeared to be motivated by stronger beliefs about benefits for crime prevention, public safety, and public systems, rather than for public health. Decreased support for harsh sentencing strategies for minor trafficking and possession of marijuana was mediated by weaker beliefs about benefits for public health, crime prevention, public systems, and/or public safety. Overall, this research suggests that public beliefs about the potential benefits of punitive drug sentencing help to motivate their levels of support for different sentencing strategies, which should be considered when promoting sentencing reform efforts for drug crimes.

title: Multi-mode Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling with Activity Soft-Splitting and Overlapping

detail.title: Multi-mode Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling with Activity Soft-Splitting and Overlapping
detail.abstract: In the face of global resource scarcity, the multi-mode resource-constrained project scheduling problem (MRCPSP) is critical for engineering management, with efficient solutions required for project success. This study incorporates a soft logic relationship into splitting strategy, thus designing a novel soft-splitting strategy, which is subsequently integrated with an overlapping strategy to address the MRCPSP. First, the study demonstrates the effects of different strategies and develops an integrated strategy. Second, a two-stage symmetry-breaking constraint programming algorithm is developed by integrating mode preprocessing and precedence-based symmetry elimination to optimize efficiency. Finally, the performance of the proposed strategies and algorithms is evaluated using wellestablished benchmarks. The results indicate that (1) the base constraint programming algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms across all datasets, (2) the two-stage symmetry-breaking constraint programming algorithm demonstrates superior efficiency in implementing our proposed 2 strategy, and (3) the integrated strategy provides shorter project durations than traditional strategies across all datasets. This study presents a transformative framework for resource-constrained project management and practical solutions for enhancing execution efficiency.

title: The Embodied Ethics Alignment Problem of AI

detail.title: The Embodied Ethics Alignment Problem of AI
detail.abstract: The problem of aligning artificial intelligence with human values is typically framed as a technical challenge: how to specify, learn, or constrain machine behavior so that artificial systems reliably produce ethically acceptable outcomes. This paper argues that this framing is fundamentally incomplete and omits an important aspect of moral agency. The central claim of this contribution is that ethics is not primarily a formalizable rule-set, preference ordering, or optimization target, but an emergent property of the human condition. Human moral agency arises from embodiment, affect, vulnerability, social embeddedness, teleological orientation, and the developmental formation of character. Alignment research, by contrast, usually treats ethics and moral agency as if it could be abstracted from these conditions and translated into reward functions, constraints, preference models, or oversight procedures. To capture this diagnosis, the paper introduces the concept of the Embodied Ethics Alignment Problem (EEAP): if moral agency depends on the embodied, affective, social, and teleological aspects of the human condition, then systems that lack those aspects cannot be ethically aligned in the "strong sense" often implied by the alignment discourse. They may be behaviorally steered toward acceptable outcomes (in the "weak sense"), but that is not the same as sharing or instantiating human moral agency. Furthermore, due to the EEAP, artificial agents may face a hard limit in terms of simulation capabilities of embodied ethics. The paper, therefore, argues that the primary task is, therefore, not to build moral machines, but to govern non-moral optimization systems within human institutions capable of bearing ethical responsibility.

title: Does Limiting Addictive Behaviors in Minors Increase Activity in Adulthood? An Empirical Study of Chinese Government Regulation on Youth Video Gaming
affiliations: School of Management, Jinan University, Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business, , Beijing Normal University (BNU) - School of Economics and Business Administration, Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business  and Singapore Management University

detail.title: Does Limiting Addictive Behaviors in Minors Increase Activity in Adulthood? An Empirical Study of Chinese Government Regulation on Youth Video Gaming
detail.abstract: Governments are beginning to take actions to restrict children’s access to social media. Psychological reactance theory implies that people may be even more eager to embrace social media after a prolonged period of restriction. To test this hypothesis, the authors examine similar regulations to restrict minors’ video gaming activity, specifically a recent Chinese regulation to curb minors’ video gaming activity. Through an online experiment and empirical analysis of data from a leading Chinese video game developer, they show that psychological reactance due to regulation increases minors’ gaming activity after they become adults. The effect is stronger for more active users before the regulation and those restricted for a longer duration, as well as for those facing greater academic pressure. The findings suggest that a thorough design to mitigate the psychological reactance is warranted in regulation policy.

title: Angry Monster: Feedback Blockage, Symbolic Protection, and the Reproduction of Abusive Supervisory Behavior
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Angry Monster: Feedback Blockage, Symbolic Protection, and the Reproduction of Abusive Supervisory Behavior
detail.abstract: This study theoretically examines why abusive supervisory behavior remains uncorrected and becomes imitated and reproduced within organizations. It focuses on three interrelated mechanisms: upward feedback blockage, symbolic protection, and mimetic reproduction of anger. Previous research has examined hostile supervisory behavior through frameworks such as abusive supervision, petty tyranny, workplace bullying, and power harassment, showing that such behavior negatively affects subordinates’ psychological well-being, job satisfaction, turnover intentions, and organizational commitment. However, less attention has been paid to why abusive managerial behavior persists over long periods, remains uncorrected despite complaints or turnover, and becomes imitated by other organizational members. This study defines the managerial condition generated through these processes as the “Angry Monster.” The term does not refer to an inherently angry individual or a pathological personality. Rather, it is used as an analytical concept to describe a supervisory condition in which abusive managerial behavior becomes difficult to correct and is reproduced within the organization because corrective signals from subordinates are blocked, the supervisor is symbolically protected by upper levels or the organization, and anger-based behavior is imitated by others. First, this paper examines upward feedback blockage under unidirectional evaluation systems. In such systems, dissent, complaints, improvement proposals, and evaluations from subordinates to supervisors are weakened in practice. Subordinates may remain silent because they fear negative evaluation, retaliation, relational deterioration, or disadvantage in assignment. This silence can then be misrecognized by supervisors as agreement, compliance, or successful control. Second, this study examines symbolic protection, which emerges when a particular manager becomes associated with organizational success narratives, legitimacy, diversity, reform, contribution, succession, or awards. Under such conditions, criticism of that person may be reinterpreted not as ordinary feedback on managerial behavior but as an attack on the symbol itself. Third, the paper analyzes how anger that is neither corrected nor challenged may be observed by other members as effective behavior and reproduced within the organization through secondary anger carriers. The theoretical contribution of this study is to redefine abusive supervisory behavior not merely as a matter of personality or emotional regulation, but as a structural phenomenon generated at the intersection of evaluation structures, symbolic structures, and mimetic structures. Building on prior work on untouchable symbols, this study clarifies how a symbolically protected supervisor may become an Angry Monster and reproduce anger within the organization. Practically, the study suggests that harassment prevention cannot rely solely on individual warnings or training. Organizations must institutionalize upward feedback, limit symbolic protection, and intervene in cultural processes that reward and reproduce anger. The conclusion of this study can be summarized as follows: the Angry Monster is not a monster simply because it gets angry. It becomes a monster because its anger cannot be stopped, is protected, is imitated, and is reproduced. Therefore, stopping the Angry Monster does not mean merely silencing one angry supervisor. It means changing the structures that fail to stop anger, protect anger, and teach others to imitate anger.

detail.abstract: As the 2026 definitive phase of the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) approaches, the global semiconductor value chain-particularly its petrochemical upstream-encounters a critical conflict between regulatory transparency and data sovereignty. This article explores the strategic orchestration of trustworthy data using the International Data Spaces (IDSA) framework. It distinguishes the mandatory, product-level requirements of CBAM from voluntary corporate pledges like the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), while addressing the additive complexities of the Safe-and-Sustainableby-Design (SSbD) framework. Focusing on the vital semiconductor-petrochemical nexus involving Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) and high-purity solvents, we highlight the role of major Asian producers-using PETRONAS, LCY Chemical, Formosa Plastics etc. as major stakeholders-in pioneering sovereign data exchange between semiconductor and petrochemical sectors. We propose the establishment of regional IDSA hubs in Taipei and Penang to catalyze a new era of "RegTech Manufacturing Services." The discussion forecasts a significant workforce evolution, identifying the shift from traditional legal and engineering roles to cross-functional "Data Sovereignty Architects" and "Semantic Interoperability Engineers" within Global Business Services (GBSs). Finally, the article explores the horizon of Agentic AI and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as tools for autonomous compliance, offering a blueprint for other global industrial clusters to achieve smart, sustainable and scalable semiconductor manufacturing.

title: Determinants of Quiet Quitting Among Generation Z and Organizational Strategies for Mitigation: A Systematic Review
affiliations: , Mindanao State University – General Santos City, Mindanao State University – General Santos City, Mindanao State University – General Santos City, Mindanao State University – General Santos City and Mindanao State University-General Santos, Philippines

detail.title: Determinants of Quiet Quitting Among Generation Z and Organizational Strategies for Mitigation: A Systematic Review
detail.abstract: Quiet quitting has become a notable post-pandemic workplace shift. Gen Z awareness is rising, yet definitions and metrics remain inconsistent. This narrative review synthesizes peer-reviewed English studies published after 2020, located via Google Scholar, Scopus, and ResearchGate. Guided by PICo, it organizes evidence on Gen Z employees (Population), quiet quitting/disengagement behaviors (Interest), and workplace conditions shaping them (Context). Most studies define quiet quitting as deliberately limiting effort to formal duties, withdrawing extra role, voluntary contributions, rather than planning to resign. It is often interpreted as boundary setting and coping with stress and burnout. Common theoretical links among Job Demands-Resources, Conservation of Resources, and Social Exchange suggest that sustained demands, scarce resources, and perceived psychological-contract breaches lead employees to recalibrate effort. Gen Z perspectives highlight work and life boundaries, fairness, recognition, value alignment, and career growth; digital work intensity and hybrid arrangements may further direct disengagement. Documented outcomes include lower organizational citizenship behaviors, higher turnover intention, and reduced performance, while also revealing deeper organizational dysfunction. Recommended responses emphasize an integrated approach: supportive leadership, timely feedback, equitable workloads, psychological safety, and clear development pathways within reciprocal employment relationships.

The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence in legal practice has produced a nationwide surge in judicial sanctions, most prominently for the submission of fabricated legal authorities. This Article presents the first comprehensive survey of judicial responses to AI-assisted legal misconduct, analyzing over one hundred sanctions decisions issued between 2023 and 2026 across more than sixty federal and state jurisdictions, supplemented by empirical analysis of a database cataloging 789 cases of AI-related misconduct in American courts. It traces the evolution of courts' approaches from early educational warnings to sophisticated detection methods, standardized sanctions, and prophylactic rules requiring disclosure and verification of AI use.

Across jurisdictions, courts uniformly reject any "AI exception" to professional responsibility. Applying existing frameworks-principally Fed. R. Civ. P. 11 and Model Rules of Professional Conduct 1.1, 3.3, and 5.1-courts hold that the duty to verify legal authority is nondelegable and that conscious avoidance of verification constitutes bad faith. The empirical data reveal a three-tiered hierarchy of harm-from fabricated legal citations to fabricated record evidence to fabricated physical evidence-with sanctions escalating correspondingly. Synthesizing sanctionable conduct, rationales, and severity factors, the Article demonstrates a clear national consensus: AI may assist lawyers, but it does not diminish professional responsibility, and failure to verify AI-generated work now carries predictable, escalating, and nationwide consequences.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to augment expert decision making, yet little is known about whether interacting with AI improves human capability beyond the period of use. We study this question using a multi-stage experiment involving radiologists diagnosing lung nodules from chest CT images. Physicians first diagnose cases without AI assistance, are then randomly assigned to diagnose cases with or without AI support and finally diagnose additional cases after AI assistance is removed. The results show that AI assistance improves contemporaneous performance, increasing diagnostic accuracy and confidence while reducing decision time. More importantly, physicians previously exposed to AI perform better even after AI assistance is removed, including on new cases, suggesting learning spillovers from AI exposure. We further find that these effects depend not only on physicians' capability but also on their self-evaluation of expertise: physicians with lower self-evaluation benefit significantly more from AI assistance and exhibit larger post-AI learning improvements. These findings suggest that AI decision support exhibits dynamic complementarity with human expertise. Beyond augmenting human performance, AI may function as a learning technology that enhances human decision capability over time.

detail.abstract: Hypodermic needles recovered from communal laundry filters in a residential building in Palermo, Buenos Aires, linked to the death of anesthesiology resident Sebastián Zalazar by propofol/fentanyl overdose (Expediente N o 8922/2026), constitute a specific diagnostic object: the terminal residue of a containment system that has already failed at every prior node. This paper argues that the needle in a dryer filter functions as a biomarker of operational spillage-the point at which a regulated pharmacological chain (hospital dispensation, controlled use, sharps disposal) has lost structural integrity and begun discharging waste into civilian space. The analytical framework departs from the needle as object and reconstructs the chain backwards: use, improvised storage, pocketing, clothing contamination, forgetting, laundering. Each step indexes a prior failure. The "otra vez?!" registered in the building's WhatsApp group transforms the finding from isolated accident to documented temporal pattern, producing involuntary distributed forensic logging by residents who did not know they were auditing anything. The case illustrates how the failure of hospital containment systems can produce detectable operational residues in non-clinical communal environments.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems deployed at global scale make consequential decisions affecting billions of people across vastly different cultural, religious, and philosophical contexts. Existing AI ethics frameworks, the preponderance of which have been authored by Western academic and regulatory institutions, encode a narrow slice of humanity's accumulated moral wisdom. The result is a structural legitimacy gap: systems calibrated to the standards of one tradition may be profoundly misaligned by those of another, with no principled mechanism for adjudicating the difference. This paper introduces AramDB, the Aram Morality Database, a structured, machine-queryable database of AI moral rulings synthesized from seven of humanity's most enduring ethical traditions: the Thirukkural (Tamil virtue ethics), Confucian role ethics, the teachings of Jesus, Daoist naturalism, Buddhist non-harm, Ubuntu relational ethics, and the Islamic maqasid framework. These seven traditions were selected on three independent criteria: geographic and civilizational diversity spanning South Asia, East Asia, West Asia, and sub-Saharan Africa; demonstrated longevity and textual stability, with each tradition maintaining a continuous practice and commentary record of at least twelve centuries; and thematic coverage of the ten moral domains most germane to contemporary AI deployment. Taken together, they constitute the ethical inheritance of an estimated 6.5 billion living persons. AramDB v0.1.0 contains ten founding rulings across ten domains. Each ruling is structured as a consensus verdict derived from a ranked tradition consultation chain-the Moral Reasoning System (MRS)-and rendered as a typed, actionable agent directive with full tradition attribution. The database is operationally deployable in its present form: any AI pipeline can load it as a JSON dependency and execute moral queries at runtime. Unlike the principle-based frameworks that dominate the current literature, AramDB produces decisions, not values statements. We invite critique, correction, and collaboration from ethicists, engineers, policymakers, and tradition scholars worldwide.

detail.abstract: Veterans enrolled in the Veterans Health Administration possess a statutory entitlement to timely, high-quality mental health care. In practice, that entitlement is not delivered uniformly. Veterans whose lives involve routine interstate mobility — including those in transportation occupations, rural and border-region residents, veterans experiencing housing instability, and recently separated service members — frequently lose continuity of care when their established community care providers lose jurisdictional authority upon crossing a state line. This paper identifies the structural source of that failure: the contractor exclusion at 38 C.F.R. § 17.417(b)(2)(iii), which extends federal licensure preemption to VA-employed clinicians but not to mental health providers delivering care through the Veterans Community Care Program (VCCP). The paper analyzes the exclusion against the current text of 38 U.S.C. § 1730C, the Department's own rulemaking record across three notice-and-comment cycles, the enacted record of Congress's FY2024 and FY2025 National Defense Authorization Acts, the interpretive divergence between the Department of Veterans Affairs and the Department of Defense on materially identical statutory authority, and the Department's affirmative obligations under Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act. A structural analysis of the Department's Veterans Integrated Service Network architecture identifies a category of agency-induced cross-state mobility — generated by the Department's own specialty care assignment practices — that sharpens the disability accommodation analysis. Three simultaneously available reform tracks are identified: regulatory amendment of § 17.417, legislative amendment of 38 U.S.C. § 1730C, and judicial review of a petition denial under the reasoned-decisionmaking standard of Motor Vehicle Manufacturers Ass'n v. State Farm. A nine-recommendation reform agenda addresses the preemption gap, bridge-care reimbursement, network adequacy, consult accountability, mobility-aware data infrastructure, and national coordination. The paper is derived from a Petition for Rulemaking filed with the Department of Veterans Affairs on May 15, 2026, pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 553(e).

detail.abstract: This paper examines the application of machine learning techniques to improve operational efficiency in large-scale digital platform environments. It develops a predictive analytics framework to estimate enforcement likelihood within platform compliance workflows, enabling more effective prioritization of high-risk cases. Using a synthetic dataset calibrated to publicly available transparency reports and platform-level disclosures, the study implements logistic regression and random forest classification models based on features such as violation category, platform type, jurisdictional capacity, and historical enforcement patterns.The empirical results demonstrate strong predictive performance, with the logistic regression model achieving an AUC-ROC of 0.81 and the random forest classifier achieving 0.87 on held-out test data. A counterfactual simulation shows that integrating predictive prioritization into operational workflows can significantly improve response efficiency by enabling earlier identification and triage of highprobability cases.The findings highlight the potential of machine learning-driven decision support systems in optimizing large-scale operational processes and contribute to the literature on business analytics, operations management, and applied machine learning in digital systems.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are moving from assistive tools into enterprise workflows where software agents retrieve information, call tools, draft artifacts, execute bounded actions, and ask for human intervention when risk rises. Written from a practitioner-scholar perspective, this paper reviews empirical evidence, technical design patterns, governance standards, and labor-market research relevant to AI-driven autonomous enterprises and the future of work by 2026. The paper's central argument is uncomfortable for firms that want a clean maturity roadmap: there is no smooth path from copilot to autonomous enterprise, because AI capability is jagged rather than uniform, and organizations that ignore this tend to automate confidently into exactly the tasks where AI fails. Evidence from randomized experiments and field studies shows substantial task-level productivity gains in writing, customer support, consulting, and programming; it also shows performance degradation outside validated task boundaries and heavy dependence on workflow redesign. Labor-market evidence indicates high exposure of occupations and tasks to generative AI, while macroeconomic effects remain uncertain and contingent on whether AI complements workers, substitutes for tasks, or enables new work. The review synthesizes this evidence into the concept of frontier-conditioned autonomy, a non-linear maturity model, an enterprise control architecture, an ethics and risk taxonomy, a value-accounting framework, and a research agenda. The highest-value autonomous enterprises by 2026 will not be those that maximize automation alone, but those that map AI's jagged frontier, preserve human responsibility for consequential decisions, measure business and human outcomes, and embed governance into enterprise platforms.

title: A HYBRID MACHINE LEARNING AND TWO-STAGE STOCHASTIC OPTIMIZATION FRAMEWORK FOR COLD-CHAIN LOGISTICS UNDER OUTBREAK SCENARIOS – A CASE STUDY IN VETERINARY CLINICS

detail.title: A HYBRID MACHINE LEARNING AND TWO-STAGE STOCHASTIC OPTIMIZATION FRAMEWORK FOR COLD-CHAIN LOGISTICS UNDER OUTBREAK SCENARIOS – A CASE STUDY IN VETERINARY CLINICS
detail.abstract: Veterinary biological cold chains under disease outbreak conditions face a fundamental planning failure: clinic-level demand becomes nonlinear, spatially heterogeneous, and epidemiologically driven, rendering conventional deterministic pre-positioning structurally inadequate. This study addresses this gap by proposing a novel integrated decision-support framework that directly couples a hybrid LSTM–XGBoost–Random Forest forecasting ensemble with a two-stage stochastic mixed-integer linear programme and an ALNS–MILP–SA matheuristic. The key methodological contribution lies in the end-to-end pipeline architecture, wherein forecast uncertainty propagates into stochastic optimisation constraints rather than being discarded at the modelling boundary, a design not previously implemented in veterinary cold-chain contexts. Applied to a feline blood distribution network across 100 veterinary clinics in Ho Chi Minh City, the framework achieves a 49.5% reduction in total expected logistics cost while sustaining full service continuity across all five epidemiological demand scenarios. Sensitivity analysis yields three actionable decision rules: an epidemic index threshold of 0.6 as a proactive fleet reallocation trigger, a cost-optimal service level of 98% that strictly dominates the conventional 95% benchmark, and a structural routing transition from consolidated tours toward high-frequency micro-dispatch as outbreak severity escalates. Expected Value of Perfect Information analysis further establishes that scenario-level epidemic foresight would be worth up to USD 87,466 per planning cycle, providing a concrete economic benchmark for investment in regional veterinary surveillance infrastructure. The Value of the Stochastic Solution further confirms that the proposed stochastic framework strictly dominates deterministic planning, with penalty costs concentrated under outbreak scenarios that a deterministic policy cannot hedge against.

title: Crisis-Alpha and Structural Decorrelation: BLT Engine Empirical Validation Across Market Regimes (2008–2025)

detail.title: Crisis-Alpha and Structural Decorrelation: BLT Engine Empirical Validation Across Market Regimes (2008–2025)
detail.abstract: We document a systematic trading strategy exhibiting three empirically anomalous properties across seventeen annual periods spanning 2008–2025: near-zero market beta (β̄ = 0.037, p = 0.540), positive compounding through every major market crisis (+41% in 2008, +45% in 2020), and regime-invariant decorrelation statistically indistinguishable across crisis and normal periods (p = 0.558). Operating exclusively in mean-reverting instruments (five major FX pairs and two precious metals ETFs), the strategy grew $1.00 to $3.94 over seventeen years without active hedging, leverage, or period-specific parameter optimization. Four complementary validation methodologies — bootstrap confidence intervals (n = 10,000), permutation tests, Monte Carlo equity curve simulation, and regime-conditional analysis — confirm that the zero-beta property is structural rather than statistical: it arises from instrument universe construction, not from offsetting exposures or averaging effects. The actual cumulative return falls at the 50.7th percentile of 10,000 Monte Carlo simulations, ruling out favorable sequencing. A statistically significant convexity property is documented (r = 0.620, p = 0.008): performance improves monotonically with market volatility, generating highest returns precisely when traditional portfolios suffer most. Sortino ratios exceed Sharpe ratios in 11 of 13 profitable periods, confirming structural return asymmetry. These findings provide the empirical foundation for the structural decorrelation hypothesis developed in the companion theoretical paper (Boutgajouft, 2026b, SSRN), which examines the implications for the CAPM, the Efficient Market Hypothesis, and multi-factor asset pricing frameworks.

detail.abstract:
The deployment of production-grade AI systems in regulated financial markets requires data infrastructure that is simultaneously low-latency, manipulation-resistant, deterministic, and operationally resilient. While model-level advances in machine learning for finance have been extensively studied, the engineering of the underlying data infrastructure layer — the true bottleneck in production AI deployments — has received comparatively little systematic treatment. This paper addresses that gap through a practitioner-grounded analysis of three recurring infrastructure failure modes across large-scale regulated financial environments: latency misalignment between model assumptions and data delivery, data normalization debt across heterogeneous sources, and observability gaps at the data ingestion layer.

The analysis draws on nearly six years of direct experience designing and operating AI-enhanced risk and connectivity systems at Nasdaq — where the Risk Platform served real-time operations for over 100 major institutional clients across North American broker-dealers and trading platforms — culminating in the role of Director of Client Integrations and AI Functionality from 2023 to 2025. The Nasdaq environment demanded regulatory-grade auditability and zero-downtime reliability at institutional scale, providing the operational laboratory in which the architectural principles developed in this paper were tested and refined.

The architectural solutions developed and validated in this environment — event-driven streaming with deterministic validation layers, hybrid GPU-accelerated inference with regulatory audit trails, and multi-layer observability focused on input quality rather than model outputs alone — are presented as transferable design patterns for production AI infrastructure in regulated settings. These patterns are further empirically validated through their application in the design of Xentaura, an institutional-grade cryptocurrency benchmarking platform built by the author. Over twelve months of live production operation, Xentaura processed over 500,000 market observations across three index tiers, maintained 99.9% uptime, and executed 24 scheduled rebalancing events without interruption — demonstrating that infrastructure principles proven at institutional scale transfer reliably to next-generation digital asset environments.

title: Blockchain Technology in the Food Industry: A Review of Potentials, Challenges and Future Research Directions

detail.title: Blockchain Technology in the Food Industry: A Review of Potentials, Challenges and Future Research Directions
detail.abstract: Blockchain technology has emerged as a promising technology with far-reaching implications for the food industry. The combination of immutability, enhanced visibility, transparency and data integrity provides numerous benefits that improve trust in extended food supply chains (FSCs). Blockchain can enhance traceability, enable more efficient recall and aids in risk reduction of counterfeits and other forms of illicit trade. Moreover, blockchain can enhance the integrity of credence claims such as sustainably sourced, organic or faith-based claims such as kosher or halal by integrating the authoritative source of the claim (e.g., the certification body or certification owner) into the blockchain to verify the claim integrity and reassure business customers and end consumers. Despite the promises and market hype, a comprehensive overview of the potential benefits and challenges of blockchain in FSCs is still missing. To bridge this knowledge gap, we present the findings from a systematic review and bibliometric analysis of sixty-one (61) journal articles and synthesize existing research. The main benefits of blockchain technology in FCSs are improved food traceability, enhanced collaboration, operational efficiencies and streamlined food trading processes. Potential challenges include technical, organizational and regulatory issues. We discuss the theoretical and practical implications of our research and present several ideas for future research.

title: The Liberating Effect of AI in Organizations
affiliations: University of New York in Tirana (UNYT)

detail.title: The Liberating Effect of AI in Organizations
detail.abstract: In the evolving landscape of organizational dynamics, AI emerges not as a usurper of human roles, but as a liberator, unshackling the human workforce from the confines of monotonous and mechanized tasks. This paper delves into a nuanced exploration of the harmonious coexistence of AI and human ingenuity, positing that AI's takeover of routine tasks paves the way for enhanced human contribution in organizations. We meticulously examine three cardinal domains of unassailable human predominance: the richness of human experience, intricate tapestry of intersubjective relations, and profound depths of symbolism and identity. Each domain was dissected, illustrating the irreplaceable nature of human touch and the ensuing enrichment of organizational culture and performance. In conclusion, we propose a counternarrative to the dystopian discourse of AI as a displacer of the human workforce. We assert that AI, in its mechanized precision, liberates human creativity and innovation, fostering an environment in which human potential is not subjugated but is unleashed, accentuated, and celebrated. We argue that this infusion of human essence will redefine organizational success and innovation, making them not just technologically advanced but also richly humanized, creative, and value-centric.

title: The Authority Gap: What the Gulf's Extraordinary Transformation Required, What It Silently Deferred, and What Artificial Intelligence Is Now Demanding in Return Front Matter

detail.title: The Authority Gap: What the Gulf's Extraordinary Transformation Required, What It Silently Deferred, and What Artificial Intelligence Is Now Demanding in Return Front Matter
detail.abstract:
Within a single human lifetime, Gulf societies built sovereign wealth funds managing assets equivalent to the GDP of Germany and positioned themselves at the frontier of the AI era. They did it by importing expertise they could not yet grow. The bargain was rational. The governance architecture mandating its completion — contractual knowledge-transfer, sunset clauses, the framework distinguishing genuine institutional authority from headcount — was never built.

Five decades of nationalisation programmes measured headcount while the coordination substrate beneath it went unmeasured. Four mechanisms institutionalised external expertise's indispensability: credential barriers functioning as directional valves; readiness narratives deferring advancement through unfalsifiable verdicts — "not yet ready" — incontestable for absence of criteria and timelines; process labyrinths whose navigational knowledge is held exclusively within the external authority cohort; and network self-replication, through which authority positions are filled from the departing incumbent's network. The legal-employment architecture sustaining all four is named here as the upper-tier kafala — a structural parallel to the working-class sponsorship system, operating through cognitive rather than physical control.

The mechanisms are not merely structural. They are semantic. "Executive presence," "strategic depth," "culture fit" — developed in the post-war Anglo-American corporate environment, validated on Western population samples, imported as universal capability standard. Never universal. Post-imperial coordination logic in organisational psychology form, enforcing conformity through the language of developmental inadequacy. The standard is the lie.

Nine national professionals at one institution held ninety-four combined years of service at the same grade. The GCC executive search industry — valued at US$50.5 billion in 2022, projected at US$148 billion by 2031 — has built its commercial existence on the narrative that capable national candidates cannot be found. McKinsey's 2024 survey: 73% of GCC organisations piloted generative AI; only 11% realised measurable value. Not a single GCC hub appears in WIPO's 2024 top 100 science and technology clusters. The implementation gap is not technological. It is the consequence of fifty years of coordination intelligence suppression.

AI makes this reckoning unavoidable — in both directions. It absorbs the procedural expertise that justified the external professional's position, leaving intact the coordination intelligence nationals have always contributed: legitimacy anchoring, institutional embeddedness, fiduciary accountability. Simultaneously, Arabic-language AI whose highest-quality expression requires nationally-embedded researchers is the first institutional intelligence technology constitutively sovereign rather than externally dependent. For the first time, the dependency's continuation is not merely unjust. It is institutionally suboptimal.

The paper proposes a governance architecture: a seven-indicator measurement framework replacing headcount; the Lateral Mastery Pathway building coordination intelligence through cross-functional accountability; the Co-Authority Model structuring every authority position as a knowledge transfer partnership with a defined succession timeline; the Cognitive Capability Assessment Framework — AI-assisted, Arabic-language-calibrated — making "not yet ready" a testable hypothesis; the Competency Sovereignty Framework returning the definition of readiness to the national professional community; and the National Talent Governance Board with board-level standing and public reporting obligations. Four falsifiable predictions specify what evidence would require the framework's revision.

The GCC funds AI infrastructure globally, anchors sovereign compute, and supplies the material substrate of the AI era — facing this pivot with an authority gap that, if not closed in this decade, will produce in the AI era exactly what it produced in the oil era: a civilisation that supplied the world's most strategically consequential resource without governing the institutions through which that resource was managed. The bargain can be completed. The decade it must be has already begun.

detail.abstract: This paper shows the declining trend in internal migration in the United States is primarily due to increasing home attachment in “fast locations,” areas with relatively high rates of population turnover. These locations were population growth destinations in the 20th century, with transient populations that settled as regional population growth converged. The qualitative patterns of the U.S. experience can be generated by a model of location choice in heterogeneous regions with overlapping generations when the population has a home bias that varies endogenously with the history of population change. Using a novel measure of home attachment, this paper estimates a structural model of migration that distinguishes moving frictions from home utility. Simulations quantify channels of the mobility decline. Rising home attachment accounts for much of the decline, predominantly in fast locations. Population aging explains most of the remainder but in a more spatially neutral way.
